svg.text: How search works in Python vs Node
One index, two readers. Same ids, same order, same band -- and the places Node is a SUBSET on purpose.
a twin module -- both runtimes
PYTHON ONLY -- no Node twin
deliberate asymmetry, not a gap
neither runtime -- removed or out of scope
0 - ONE INDEX. THE COMMITTED BYTES ARE THE WHOLE CONTRACT.
.fux/index/*.jsonl shards + sources/dirs + formats.toml + tune.toml + output.toml + identifiers.toml + pii.toml + fux.toml
Statistics about documents, never the documents (fux.index.v7, analyzer v3, 256 shard buckets). Python writes every one of these; both readers
read them, the pins `fux correct` files, the gitignored .fux/runtime/ plane and .fux/acquired/ -- and nothing else.
No server, no model, no clock, no network on the query path in either runtime.
Python `fux` -- pip install fux-engine (3.0.0-alpha.10)
50 117 lines of .py in src/fux. 24 verbs; Node implements 9 of them.
THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: when the two disagree, this one is right
by definition. It writes the index (ingest) and every committed .fux/ file.
Python >= 3.12 (L7). Decoders, fetchers, redaction, enrichment: here only.
Node `fux` -- npm i fux-engine, vendored to .fux/node/
8 875 lines of .mjs in node/src. 8 read verbs -- find ask lexical answer
explain graph path mcp -- and build, the one thing Node writes (W-242).
The other 15 are refused and signpost the Python binary.
Node >= 22 (L8). Zero dependencies; the bundle is L10's. Answers a clone with no Python.
1 - THE SHARED QUERY PIPELINE: FIFTEEN TWINS, ONE PER MODULE, AT THE SAME RELATIVE PATH (query/y.mjs -> src/fux/query/y.py)
tokenize.py / tokenize.mjs
42 / 13 lines. The one place a query becomes terms.
stem.py / stem.mjs
210 / 183. Suffix rules, transcribed rule for rule.
analyzer.py + identifiers.py / .mjs
200 / 135 and 524 / 329. Term hashes, order PRESERVED; identifier families
from .fux/identifiers.toml kept whole. One fixture, read by both suites (W-202).
expand.py + mined.py / .mjs
168 / 79 and 157 / 72. --expand: the CALLER's words, never an invented term;
mined.json pairs folded from the corpus itself (W-168 step 4). lexical: weight 0.
scan.py / scan.mjs
288 / 179. THE DEFAULT PATH. Every shard line read as raw bytes, ONCE per call;
flen and mtime by regex; a line is parsed only if it substring-matches a hash.
bm25f.py + rank.py + intent.py / .mjs
263 / 134, 496 / 188, 110 / 78. guard -> BM25F -> multipliers (archived,
priority, intent prior, pin) -> sort. Scoring lives here in both, never in
the candidate generator, so the two cannot drift.
fuse.py / fuse.mjs
96 / 52. -q -> reciprocal rank fusion.
rerank.py / rerank.mjs
338 / 239. Proximity rerank -- OFF unless rerank_weight > 0.
compose.py / compose.mjs
346 / 240. The graph tier -- `ask` only; `lexical` forces it off. Needs the
derived plane: Python drops the tier without one, Node rebuilds it (section 4).
headings.py / headings.mjs
95 / 33. Section paths for the cited lines.
confidence.py / confidence.mjs
479 / 211. The band: grounded | weak | partial | none. answerable = band != none
(W-214): `weak` is a published signal, not a refusal.
one ranked, banded list -- identical in both runtimes
ingest/pii.py (761 lines)
The redaction engine runs at INGEST, so
both readers inherit redacted bytes.
Python owns the rules, the luhn and
verhoeff validators, the ReDoS linter
(W-255) and PII_EXEMPT.
derive/accel + format + _build
THE ACCELERATOR -- twins since W-242.
.fux/runtime/ postings, rarest-first, exact
theta, block-max bound, round(9)-aware skip.
Taken only on --fast (and on mcp) AND a
fresh stamp; else it falls through to the
scan -- never a wrong answer.
Node at 10k docs: ~0.13 s scan -> ~0.09 s (alpha.10)
query/provenance.py (1 054 lines)
--why, --receipt, --journal, and the whole
verify verdict set (reproduced | drifted:
corpus | drifted:config | unverifiable).
NO NODE TWIN AT ALL.
Declared out of scope on Node (d25, 2026-10-04):
these surfaces are uncovered by the arm, openly.
Node's gate is a STAT, not a parse.
.fux/pii.toml must exist or every verb
refuses -- one literal path in fux.mjs,
carried into the bundle. No Node twin of
PII_EXEMPT and none is needed: all four
exempt verbs (setup tune output doctor)
are Python-only.
Node reads AND builds the plane.
--fast / --scan in both runtimes. `fux build`
in Node writes Python's bytes exactly (every
file but stamp.json), under the same
write.lock; each reads the other's plane at
0 discordant. Both MCPs report ranked_by
from the path that actually answered.
W-242, all tiers built 2026-10-03. ranked_by is
compared by the arm now, not excluded by name.
Node reads tune.toml + output.toml.
Closed 2026-09-12. Before it, a tuned repo
ranked DIFFERENTLY in the two readers with
nothing saying so: 90 of 174 discordant.
After: 0 of 199. --no-tune is a two-runtime
flag, or it is not the switch it claims.
tune.mjs 534 / tune.py 751 (the reader half);
output.mjs 491 / output_config.py 695.
2 - THREE PYTHON SEMANTICS THE NODE READER REIMPLEMENTS -- each one is a correctness fix, not a nicety
round(x, 9) is half-EVEN
on the exact binary value. toFixed(9)
is half-UP and fails exactly on ties --
and a tie resolved the other way is a
DIFFERENT ORDER.
repr(float) exponent thresholds
Python switches at e < -4 or e >= 16;
JS at -6 / 21. Both shortest-round-trip,
so only the printed layout differs.
cmpCodePoints on every id
Python compares by CODE POINT, JS by
UTF-16 code UNIT. The sort key ends in id,
so one emoji reorders results: 30 of 324
ordered pairs disagreed, measured.
Five Node files therefore have NO Python twin, and the exemption list is short on purpose -- it is exactly where divergence risk concentrates (SR-NODE-SEARCH d6):
hash/blake2b.mjs (hashlib is out of reach) | compat/pyfloat.mjs | compat/pyjson.mjs (json.dumps, byte for byte -- W-242) | config/toml.mjs (tomllib IS the twin) | verbs/*.mjs (one-to-many).
Since W-225 (L12) blake2b.mjs and pyfloat.mjs hold no numeral: RFC 7693's tables and CPython's repr thresholds are read from src/fux/constants.toml, inlined into the bundle.
3 - THE REFER PLANE (`fux answer`) -- where the two readers genuinely part company
Shared twins -- ranking has already chosen the documents before any of this runs, so nothing here changes WHICH document is cited, only which passage.
A leading frontmatter block is passage 0 in both (W-254). Three Python halves are private modules (`_chunk.py` -> `chunk.mjs`): the twin rule's `_y.py` form.
_chunk.py / .mjs
565 / 285 lines
_rescore.py / .mjs
198 / 107 lines
_assemble.py / .mjs
197 / 85 lines
source.py / .mjs
193 / 69 lines
freshness.py / .mjs
263 / 53 lines
IN PYTHON ONLY
decode/ -- 17 built-in decoders + .fux/decoders/*.py
csv docx drawio html image ini json jsonl mail pdf pptx rtf svg toml xlsx xml
yaml. A consumer decoder is arbitrary Python; there can be no Node twin, ever.
refer/arc.py (142) -- the (loc, sha) ARC content cache
refer/fetchcache.py (183) -- the TTL url cache, runtime/fetch-cache/
fetchers -- http.py, the signed-in-Chrome cdp.py; refusals.toml
store/acquired.py (353) -- the writer of .fux/acquired/
Node's decode/ is TWO files: registry.mjs, which answers one question (is this
already text?), and markdown.mjs. Nothing else, and nothing planned.
WHAT NODE DOES INSTEAD
Node has NO TRANSPORT. Not off by default -- there is no
fetcher seam and nothing to inject one through (d3).
file: reads the working tree (your own checkout is not a fetch).
url: reads .fux/acquired/objects/<sha> if retained, else source: "index".
[sources.url] fetch_at_answer = false makes Python do the same (W-174).
A document that needs a DECODER is DECLINED, not guessed at (d11).
The question asked is never "does a decoder claim this extension?"
but "is this ALREADY TEXT?" -- which formats.toml's include list
answers in committed bytes both runtimes read. Under-claiming is the
only safe direction: a wrong citation vs the next candidate.
So the url: freshness verdict set is ASYMMETRIC, deliberately (SR-NODE-SEARCH d4; the vocabulary is SR-URL-FRESHNESS's)
verdict
PYTHON
NODE
why
current / stale
file: and url:
file: ONLY
Node cannot look at a URL
as-ingested
yes
yes
the acquired blob is local
unverified
yes
yes
we did not look
cached
yes
NEVER
a TTL fetch cache requires fetching
Node reporting `current` for a URL it never
checked would make the claim-strength vocabulary
mean different things in two runtimes -- the one
thing SR-URL-FRESHNESS exists to prevent.
A DECISION. NOT A GAP.
4 - THE THIRD ASYMMETRY: THE DERIVED GRAPH PLANE -- Python REFUSES without it; Node reads it when fresh and rebuilds otherwise
Python: graph/plane.py::load (130 lines)
Reads the derived .fux/runtime/graph.json and REFUSES
when it is absent or stale (accel.is_fresh, the one staleness
rule). explain / graph / path need a fresh `fux build` -- Python's
or Node's; `ask` answers with no graph tier and says so on stderr.
Both builders write graph.json with ensure_ascii + insertion order.
Node: graph/plane.mjs::planeFor (121 lines)
Reads graph.json when accel.mjs::isFresh says it is fresh -- Fork A,
ruled 2026-10-04 and BUILT (W-259). Otherwise it rebuilds the plane IN
MEMORY from two fields of each record (id, edges) and answers either
way. Never required: a clone with no `fux build` still answers.
Read vs rebuild: byte-identical, 512 of 512. Speed vs the frozen bar: NULL (9.5 % vs 10 %).
It follows that explain / graph / path cannot be COMPARED on a corpus with no fresh build, and node_arm.py::graph_lane_ready says so out loud rather than skipping quietly;

every CI arm job runs `fux build` first (44 of 202 discordant without it, 0 of 225 with it). The arm NEVER takes Node's read: FUX_GRAPH_REBUILD=1 on every Node child, or N2 compares Python with itself.
5 - WHAT HOLDS THEM EQUAL -- a second implementation is a second thing to keep true
The differential arm: SIX surfaces since 2026-09-12 (it covered ONE before, and all three defects found that day lived on one it did not reach), plus W-242's build lane and N2
1 find 2 ask 3 explain / graph / path, whole parsed payloads 4 the MCP server, a real stdio session 5 fux.api vs index.mjs 6 the BUNDLE vs the module tree
build lane: diff -r Node-built vs Python-built, stamp.json excluded, then each answers from the OTHER's plane N2: graph_arm.py, the graph digest
Where it runs (.github/workflows/ci.yml): every push, 10 shards on Linux / Node 22; on main, nightly and dispatch, 3 OSes x Node 22 / 24 x 3 shards, this repo then the adversarial
corpus. `fux build` before every arm, FUX_GRAPH_REBUILD=1 on every Node child, --python-tune off on BOTH sides so a discordance is attributable. Latest: 0 of 801 (PRE-REG-NODE-3, W-252).
tests/test_node_twins.py maps every .mjs to its .py (x/y.mjs -> src/fux/x/y.py, or _y.py) and fails when a Python twin changes and its .mjs does not -- which the arm cannot catch.
tests/test_node_config_parity.py asserts the key sets and the REFUSALS, because a drifted refusal never shows up as a finding, only as a crash on one side (d6, d8).
One fixture, both suites: tests/query/identifier-fixture.json (the analyzer) · tests/derive/idx-fixture.* (the 62-byte .idx entry) · test_anchor_node_twin.py (anchors, W-168 step 1).
Tolerance: scores equal after round(9), the sort key's own resolution -- the api lane too since 2026-10-03. ORDERING is byte-equal and has no tolerance: a discordant top-5 fails the arm.
6 - IN NEITHER RUNTIME, OR DECLARED OUT OF SCOPE -- named so that absence is not mistaken for coverage
the vector plane
REMOVED. A dense embedding lane
fixed 0 queries and broke 2, and was
deleted; W-112 closed 2026-09-14.
No embeddings on either query path.
RM3 · the authority prior
REMOVED FROM BOTH, each in one
change (W-224 / W-237; W-168 step 8,
2026-10-03). rm3_weight is refused by
name in both loaders, same sentence.
verify --why --receipt --journal
PYTHON ONLY, declared out of scope
on Node (d25, 2026-10-04). No twin,
so the arm does not pretend to cover
them -- a stated absence, not a gap.
observers · serve · inspect
PYTHON ONLY. .fux/observers/*.mjs is
reserved and unread (d18); fux serve
and fux inspect are surfaces, and the
differential law reaches readers.
Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/query/, src/fux/refer/, src/fux/derive/, src/fux/graph/, src/fux/cli.py, node/src/, .github/workflows/ci.yml, CHANGELOG.md (3.0.0-alpha.10 + Unreleased).

Every difference not on this page is a defect. Siblings: architecture-caching.svg (the shared .fux/runtime/ plane) · architecture-ask.svg · architecture-answer.svg · architecture-cicd.svg (where the arm runs).
